tier_reason: Lowered A to C under the rule that numbers measured on code later fixed for a correctness bug go to C: the README timings are unchanged since commit 1fc2be8 (2017-09-18), and the SSE2 yuv2rgb path timed there used srai plus sub_epi8, so (Y-16)*149 overflowed int16 for BT.601/709 luma of 236 and above and those pixels came out black (issue #12); the fix e805bf2 (2022-02-09, srli plus subs_epu8) is a same-cost swap, so the timing is probably unaffected, but it was never re-run. The harness, compiler, flags and CPU remain public. Also from the enricher: the 'aligned' SSE2 path uses _mm_stream_si128 non-temporal stores (no sfence), so the 0.607 s versus 0.704 s gap is store type rather than alignment, and the plain-store SSE2 path (0.704 s) is slower than IPP (0.636 s); the test streams about 40 MB per frame from DRAM.

corrections.caveats: README timings date from 2017 code whose SSE2 yuv2rgb path had an int16 overflow (luma 236 and above decoded black, issue #12, fixed 2022-02-09); never re-run after the fix. Author's own run on one laptop CPU (i7-5500U) with an old swscale 3.0.0 (likely Libav 11 on Debian 8) whose YUV420P to RGB24 path is MMX code; modern swscale has newer SIMD paths. Intel IPP 9.0.1 beat the SSE2 code on rgb2yuv and the plain-store SSE2 yuv2rgb path (0.704 s versus 0.636 s); the 'aligned' variant's edge is _mm_stream_si128 non-temporal stores without an sfence. The swscale contexts use flags 0 and outputs are never compared, so equivalence is unchecked; the rgb2yuv gap is partly different work (swscale has no unscaled fast path for RGB24 input). Width below 31 wraps the uint32 loop (out-of-bounds); rgb32_yuv420_std still uses cb_factor for V at HEAD (issue #15 fix missed the RGBA path); unconditional emmintrin.h, so no ARM build.
